rituals.name: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.hook: The Effort Staircase: Action avoidance gets smaller here. Finish criterion: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Effort Staircase: Action avoidance gets smaller here. Finish criterion: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.

rituals.mission: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.

rituals.immediate_need: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.game_move: Name opens; Remain Version pivots. Last decision: Climb Stair.
rituals.unique_game_move: Name opens; Remain Version pivots. Last decision: Climb Stair.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
The Effort Staircase: Action avoidance gets smaller here. Finish criterion: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.

GAME MOVE
Name opens; Remain Version pivots. Last decision: Climb Stair.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name — Name five versions of the task from almost easy to genuinely stretching.
2. Cross Out — Cross out the zero-effort decoy.
3. Remain Version — Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Climb Stair — Next time, climb only one stair.

FINISH MOVE — Let Climb Stair be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The Effort Staircase proves this: start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers. Keep evidence; leave at Climb Stair.
rituals.formula_flow: Name → Cross Out → Remain Version → Climb Stair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reduce the step further if illness, exhaustion, or overload is being ignored.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
rituals.hook: Mood Has Alibis: Emotion–fact confusion gets smaller here. Only this matters: Test what the day does to the feeling.

TRIGGER
Emotional reasoning

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Mood Has Alibis: Emotion–fact confusion gets smaller here. Only this matters: Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Test what the day does to the feeling.

GAME MOVE
Choose Activity opens; Add Sentence pivots. Nothing follows Repeat Different here.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Activity — Choose one activity.
2. Score Expected — Before it, score expected mood; at the start, Notice actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add Sentence — Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Repeat Different — Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’

WIN SIGNAL

rituals.title: TWO ENGINES
rituals.name: TWO ENGINES
rituals.hook: Low energy does not always need one perfect fix. TWO ENGINES asks for one spark of enjoyment and one spark of capability, both small enough to use today.
rituals.recognition_cue: Low energy does not always need one perfect fix. TWO ENGINES asks for one spark of enjoyment and one spark of capability, both small enough to use today.
rituals.goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.mission: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.challenge: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.immediate_need: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.game_move: Schedule Chosen opens; Check Both pivots. Stopping line: Drop Demand.
rituals.unique_game_move: Schedule Chosen opens; Check Both pivots. Stopping line: Drop Demand.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Low energy does not always need one perfect fix. TWO ENGINES asks for one spark of enjoyment and one spark of capability, both small enough to use today.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.

GAME MOVE
Schedule Chosen opens; Check Both pivots. Stopping line: Drop Demand.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Two Engines proves this: pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you. Final marker: Drop Demand.
rituals.formula_flow: Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Rebalance if achievement becomes punishment or pleasure becomes avoidance.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.safety_notes:

TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Use One Visible Vote on Perfectionism. Let this change: Values become real only after the body votes.

Values become real only after the body votes.

Start Choose Value; use Complete Shift. Tiny arrives; experiment over.

3. Tiny — A tiny enacted vote outranks a perfect private speech.

WIN SIGNAL
One Visible Vote lands here: values become real only after the body votes. Stop the game at Tiny.

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Use Cool — Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
2. Slow — Slow your body while the sensation lands.
3. Remove Name — Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
4. Test Endurance — Cooling is a reset cue, not a test of endurance.

GOAL
Give body alarm a finish line.

GAME MOVE
Enter at Choose Burst; turn at End Completely. Last decision: Let Body.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Burst — Choose a contained burst: fast stairs, wall pushes, brisk marching, or another safe vigorous movement.
2. Set Short — Set a short timer before starting.
3. End Completely — When it ends, stop completely, feel the after-pulse, and drink water.
4. Let Body — Let the body spend energy without spending your future.

FINISH MOVE — Let Let Body be enough.

rituals.hook: Relief is not the only learning moment. STAY THROUGH RECOVERY keeps you present long enough to notice what your body does after the alarm crests.

rituals.game_move: Highest first. Remain Cue carries the middle. Stopping line: Follow Learning.

rituals.trigger_play_time:

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The nervous system learns more after the peak than at the exit.

GAME MOVE
Highest first. Remain Cue carries the middle. Stopping line: Follow Learning.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Highest — During a safe exposure, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Follow Learning — Departure follows learning, not panic.

FINISH MOVE — Follow Learning is your cue to stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Stay Through Recovery works if this shifts: the nervous system learns more after the peak than at the exit. Final marker: Follow Learning.

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:

Safety behaviours can hide the safety you are trying to learn.

GAME MOVE
Identify Protective first. Drop Legitimate carries the middle. Observe Outcome ends the useful part.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Protective — During a manageable exposure, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying reassurance.
2. Drop Legitimate — Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.

FINISH MOVE — Let Observe Outcome be enough.

GOAL
Self-inquiry works better as disciplined research.

GAME MOVE
4 moves: Choose Recurring into Compare Trusted. Close at Picture A Guess; do not restart.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Recurring — Choose a reaction that happens often and remember three times it happened.
2. Read Pattern — For each time, notice the trigger, meaning, body feeling, action, and result.
3. Compare Trusted — Compare the three examples with a trusted idea or guide.
4. Picture A Guess — Picture one idea to test. Do not judge your whole character.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.

GAME MOVE
Keep Scan Work small; move through Bind Object. Close at Run Command; do not restart.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Scan Work — Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check.
2. Pick Verb — Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
3. Bind Object — Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now.
4. Run Command — Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object genuinely needs to change.

Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.

GAME MOVE
Begin Emotion; no side task before State Action. Stay Blurred lands; leave it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.

FINISH MOVE — Let Stay Blurred be enough.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
One role should not own every share of self.

GAME MOVE
Begin Estimate Much; no side task before Choose Neglected. Leave it at Perform.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Estimate Much — Name five identities active in your life and estimate how much attention each received this week.
2. Choose Neglected — Choose the neglected role that still matters.
3. Perform — Perform one tiny action from its perspective today—friend, learner, neighbour, artist, caregiver, citizen.

FINISH MOVE — Perform closes Open The Identity Portfolio.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
At the end of Open The Identity Portfolio, keep this: one role should not own every share of self. Exit at Perform.
rituals.formula_flow: Estimate Much → Choose Neglected → Perform

PAUSE
Do not use role expansion to avoid urgent responsibilities in the dominant role.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

GAME MOVE
Place Memory to Keep Events; no rewind. Stop at Add Resources.

rituals.hook: Ask What The Memory Is Still Billing changes the angle on Rumination. Use this target: The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.

rituals.unique_game_move: Headline Event to Route Bill; no rewind. Exit at Act Present.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rumination & worry loops

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Ask What The Memory Is Still Billing changes the angle on Rumination. Use this target: The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.

GAME MOVE
Headline Event to Route Bill; no rewind. Exit at Act Present.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Headline Event — State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay.
2. Extract Claim — Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory is still asking for ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route Bill — Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Act Present — Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.

FINISH MOVE — Let Act Present be enough.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Ask What The Memory Is Still Billing did its job if: the memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case. Round ends at Act Present.
rituals.formula_flow: Headline Event → Extract Claim → Route Bill → Act Present
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people, seek revenge, force reconciliation, or use this game during trauma flooding or immediate danger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE LAPSE FIRE DRILL
rituals.name: THE LAPSE FIRE DRILL
rituals.hook: The Lapse Fire Drill changes the angle on Rejection magnification. Stay with this: One miss should trigger recovery, not identity collapse.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Lapse Fire Drill changes the angle on Rejection magnification. Stay with this: One miss should trigger recovery, not identity collapse.

rituals.game_move: Name What Happened to Store; no rewind. Finish at Use After; move on.
rituals.unique_game_move: Name What Happened to Store; no rewind. Finish at Use After; move on.

rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Name What Happened — Pre-plan three actions after a lapse: name what happened without judgement; restore the environment or schedule; perform the next smallest valid repetition.
2. Store — Store the script beside the behaviour.
3. Use After — Use it after one miss—before a second is negotiated.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Use After, then return to your day.

Observer loss & cognitive fusion

1–2 minutes

HOOK
At Observer loss, reach for Notice The Space Doing The Holding. Work toward: Objects dominate because intervals are treated as nothing.

Objects dominate because intervals are treated as nothing.

GAME MOVE
Choose Forms gets first beat; Reverse Figure is pivot. Do not pass Include Room.

1. Choose Forms — Choose three forms.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
The nervous system learns more after the peak than at the exit.

GAME MOVE
Highest first. Remain Cue carries the middle. Stopping line: Follow Learning.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Highest — During a safe exposure, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Follow Learning — Departure follows learning, not panic.

FINISH MOVE — Follow Learning is your cue to stop.

Begin Smallest; hinge on Ask Whether. Exit at Let Determine.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Smallest — Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
2. Pause Enlarge — Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Ask Whether — Ask whether it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
4. Let Determine — Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.

FINISH MOVE — Let Determine closes the round.

items.goal_steps_source:
GOAL
Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.

1. Name Causes — For twenty seconds, ban emotion names and causes.
2. Describe Geometry — Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
3. Choose Smallest — At the bell, choose the smallest Name that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Choose Smallest is your cue to stop.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.

items.play_the_loop:
1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.

FINISH MOVE — Let Receive Own be enough.
